title: Rotavirus vaccine
what: It is not a shot, but drops by mouth. They protect your baby from severe rotavirus infection with vomiting and diarrhea.
why: For babies in the first months of life, on the schedule. The course is usually 2 to 3 doses, and it must start on time.
duration: giving the drops takes about a minute, with the checkup usually 15 to 40 minutes
tell_doctor: If your baby is ill now, or has vomiting or diarrhea
A past bowel blockage called intussusception

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: The first dose must be given before a certain age in weeks. Do not delay. Ask your pediatrician.

prepare.title: Feeding
prepare.text: You can feed your baby as usual, before and after.

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: Your baby should be well on the day of the vaccine.

steps: The doctor examines your baby and takes their temperature
You hold your baby half sitting
The nurse puts the vaccine drops in their mouth
After the vaccine, sit in the clinic for about 30 minutes
feel: Sometimes looser stools or fussiness for a few days
after: Wash your hands after diaper changes, especially in the first week
red_flags: Bouts of hard crying, pulling up the legs, vomiting, or blood in the stool: call emergency services
Trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, or a rash all over: call emergency services

faq.q: What if my baby spits up the vaccine?
faq.a: Usually it does not need to be repeated. Tell the nurse, who will decide.
There are age limits for the first and last doses. If you are late, the doctor will decide.

reminders.text: Rotavirus vaccine tomorrow. Your baby should be well. Bring the vaccination record.
